blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: virtual storage — Remote network-accessible file storage.
virtual memory — OS technique using address translation and backing storage.
firmware — Low-level code retained without power.

blocks.title: RAM versus ROM
blocks.text: RAM supports active execution and is volatile; ROM and firmware storage retain instructions without power.

blocks.title: Define virtual storage
blocks.text: A remote or cloud storage service keeps files on network-accessible systems, potentially available on multiple devices.

blocks.title: Distinguish virtual memory
blocks.text: OS virtual memory involves memory addressing/paging with secondary storage, taught again in OS memory management.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict
blocks.text: Unsaved temporary program state depends on volatile RAM and can disappear without power.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain
blocks.text: Firmware persists in non-volatile storage, allowing startup instructions to remain available.

questions.feedback: virtual storage — Remote network-accessible file storage.

blocks.title: Predict
blocks.text: Virtual/cloud storage supports access from multiple locations and may offer remote copies.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: Network outages, account security and mistakenly synced deletions are relevant risks.
